Olga,

Thanks for the draft order form. We reviewed the MSA + order form with procurement and legal. Two items that are blockers for our procurement committee: 1) the auto-renew clause with a 60-day notice; and 2) lack of a clear, short-path termination-for-convenience for pilots.

I attached our redline of the Order Form (GF_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Can your commercial/legal teams propose language that balances Redwood's renewal economics with our need to avoid unexpected renewals? Also cc'ing Tom (procurement) who will own final signoff.

Subject: Re: Order form & MSA - proposed compromise language

Team — after reviewing Globex's redline and the account constraints, here is a recommended compromise we can present to their legal/procurement:

1) Pilot opt-out mechanics (one-time only):
- Insert clause: "Customer may elect, one time prior to the first renewal term, to opt out of auto-renewal for the subsequent period by providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Redwood. Such election may be used only once and will not apply to any subsequent renewal term unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Notice window:
- Reduce standard renewal notice in the Order Form from sixty (60) days to forty-five (45) days for customers in a pilot program (defined in the Order Form).

3) Termination & transition:
- Add a termination-for-convenience style paragraph for pilots: "In the event Customer exercises the one-time opt-out, Redwood will provide reasonable transition support for a period of sixty (60) days and will refund, on a pro-rata basis, any pre-paid fees for the unused portion of the then-current billing period."

Rationale: keeps predictable renewal cadence for enterprise customers while giving pilot customers a narrow, auditable exit path. It also limits operational churn by making the opt-out one-time.

Please note operational items we need to confirm before presenting: billing proration implementation, indicator on the account for 'pilot opt-out used' to prevent re-use, and a signal from procurement when the pilot flag is set.

If everyone agrees, I'll draft the exact redline (order form + 1-page explanatory memo) and send to Samantha.

Marissa Cole
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
